theme: Phosphate-driven mineralization of bone and teeth
story: The centre is hard-tissue mineralization: bone mineralization during maturation (with positive and negative regulation), dentinogenesis, enamel mineralization, tooth eruption, and hypomineralized amelogenesis imperfecta caused by SLC24A4 defects. The endocrine and signalling members (parathyroid hormone response, FGF23 acting through FGFR1c-Klotho, FGFR-driven MAPK signalling, response to sodium phosphate) supply the phosphate and calcium control that sets how much mineral can be laid down, while chondrocyte development and post-translational phosphorylation (which covers secreted matrix phosphoproteins) are the cellular and matrix side. Together the cluster describes how mineral homeostasis and matrix cells cooperate to calcify skeleton and dentition.

theme: MHC class I antigen processing and cross-presentation
story: The core is the MHC class I pathway: proteasomal degradation of ubiquitinated proteins, peptide transport into the ER, and folding, assembly and peptide loading of class I molecules for presentation of endogenous antigens. Cross-presentation routes (endosomal/vacuolar, ER-phagosome, phagosomal and endosomal handling of soluble and particulate antigens, cytosol-to-ER transport) extend this to exogenous antigens captured by dendritic cells, and CD8 T cell homeostasis is the downstream consumer of those peptide-MHC complexes. Vpu-mediated CD4 degradation fits as a viral hijacking of the same ER-associated proteasomal machinery; overall the cluster is about generating peptide-MHC I ligands for CD8 T cell immunity.

theme: EGFR/ERBB family receptor signalling and its downregulation
story: This is the ERBB receptor tyrosine kinase family: EGFR, ERBB2, ERBB3 and ERBB4 homo- and heterodimer signalling and the adaptor-specific branches each recruits (SHC1, GRB2, GAB1 signalosome, PI3K, PLC-gamma1, GRB7, PTK6). Supporting members cover outputs and control: ERBB2-driven cell motility, nuclear signalling by the cleaved ERBB4 intracellular domain, autophosphorylation, transactivation of EGFR by gastrin and GPER1, and downregulation or inhibition of ERBB2:ERBB3, ERBB4 and overexpressed EGFR. The cluster as a whole maps how ERBB ligands are converted into proliferative and migratory signals through shared adaptors, and how that signalling is switched off.

theme: Phase I xenobiotic and natural-product oxidative metabolism
story: The centre is xenobiotic metabolism and catabolism, carried out largely by cytochrome P450 oxidations such as CYP1A2 N-hydroxylation of aromatic amines, oxidative demethylation and aflatoxin activation/detoxification. Around it sit the classes of foreign plant and fungal compounds these enzymes handle (mycotoxins, alkaloids, phenylpropanoids, monoterpenoids, polyketides) and the alcohol dehydrogenase side of the same detoxifying machinery (ethanol oxidation, primary alcohol catabolism). Together it describes the liver's oxidative clearance of dietary and environmental chemicals, which can either detoxify or bioactivate them.

theme: Detoxification of reactive aldehydes, sulfide and protein damage
story: The clearest core is methylglyoxal and aldehyde detoxification (methylglyoxal metabolism and response, aldehyde catabolism and cellular detoxification) together with protein repair and DNA protection, which describes how glycating dicarbonyls are neutralized and how their damage to proteins and nucleic acids is reversed (e.g. by DJ-1/PARK7-type deglycases). Sulfide oxidation to sulfate and molybdenum cofactor biosynthesis, with prosthetic group metabolism, add the mitochondrial and molybdoenzyme side of handling reactive small molecules (sulfite oxidase and aldehyde oxidase depend on Moco). The cluster is loosely a cellular defence against toxic reactive metabolites, though the Moco/sulfide members join the glyoxal-repair core more by function than by shared pathway.

theme: Antimicrobial peptides and mucosal defence against bacteria and fungi
story: The centre is the antimicrobial effector arsenal of innate immunity: alpha- and beta-defensins, metal sequestration by antimicrobial proteins, cytolysis and membrane disruption of microbes, neutrophil killing of Gram-negative bacteria, bacterial agglutination, and defence against Gram-positive bacteria and fungi/yeast. Supporting members frame this at barrier surfaces and in relation to symbionts: innate immunity in mucosa, host modulation of intestinal microbiota, bacterial attachment to epithelia, responses to symbionts, and microbial cell-wall polymers (peptidoglycan, chitin) that are targeted or sensed. Together it describes how epithelia and phagocytes secrete peptides and proteins that kill or contain microbes and shape the commensal flora.

theme: Fast ionotropic synaptic transmission and presynaptic modulation
story: The core is ligand-gated ion channels that carry fast excitatory postsynaptic currents: AMPA and kainate glutamate receptors (sodium- and calcium-permeable forms, presynaptic kainate function, response to kainic acid) and neuronal nicotinic acetylcholine receptors of differing calcium and sodium permeability. The G protein side supplies inhibitory modulation, with G-beta/gamma activating GIRK potassium channels and inhibiting voltage-gated calcium channels, alongside extrasynaptic GABA signalling and regulation of presynaptic membrane potential. Together the cluster describes how excitation is generated at synapses and how neurotransmitter receptors tune release and excitability.

theme: Netrin and semaphorin-3A axon guidance
story: The centre is axon guidance by attractive and repulsive cues: netrin signalling (including netrin-mediated repulsion) and semaphorin 3A acting through plexin, CRMPs and PAK to collapse growth cones and reduce integrin adhesion. The outcome members describe what guidance does to the axon, namely positive or negative regulation of axon extension, chemorepulsion, anterior/posterior guidance, and microtubule depolymerization in the growth cone. Branching of nerves, axonogenesis for innervation and sympathetic neuron projection extension place this machinery in building peripheral nerve wiring.

theme: Telomere maintenance by telomerase and shelterin protection
story: The core is telomere replication and extension: telomerase holoenzyme assembly and recruitment (including telomerase RNA localization to Cajal bodies), telomere extension, and C-strand fill-in synthesis with polymerase switching and flap removal. The protective arm caps chromosome ends, packages telomeres, blocks non-homologous end joining and inhibits recombination at telomeres, with ATRX and DAXX mutations defining the defective-inhibition (ALT) states and t-circle formation reflecting that recombination route. Protein localization to telomeres links the two, so the cluster as a whole describes how chromosome ends are lengthened and protected from being treated as DNA breaks.

theme: Cardiac action potential and conduction system
story: The centre is electrical conduction through the heart: AV node depolarization, His bundle to Purkinje and Purkinje to ventricular myocyte communication, and regulation of heart rate by conduction. Around it are the membrane events that make each cardiomyocyte action potential, namely phase 0 rapid depolarization, regulation of atrial and ventricular depolarization and ventricular repolarization, and the coupling of the action potential to contraction. Chemical regulation of heart rate adds autonomic and humoral tuning, so the cluster describes how the cardiac impulse is generated and spread to coordinate the heartbeat.

theme: Transport and homeostasis of zinc, manganese and iron
story: The core is transmembrane transport of divalent metal ions by SLC39 (ZIP) family importers: zinc import and intracellular zinc homeostasis, response to zinc starvation, and the closely related manganese and cadmium transport, with SLC39A4 defects causing acrodermatitis enteropathica. Iron export members (ferroportin SLC40A1 defects causing hemochromatosis type 4, and ceruloplasmin loss in aceruloplasminemia) add the efflux and ferroxidase side of transition-metal handling, while cadmium detoxification reflects toxic metals entering through the same carriers. Together it describes how cells take up, distribute and export essential trace metals and the diseases that follow when those transporters fail.

theme: Testis development and spermatogenesis
story: The cluster centres on the male gonad: seminiferous tubule development, Sertoli cell proliferation and blood-testis barrier formation, and Leydig cell differentiation provide the somatic niche. The germ-line members track germ cells through that niche, from primordial germ cell migration and regulated proliferation and apoptosis, through entry into meiosis and maturation, to building the sperm midpiece mitochondrial sheath. Together it describes how the testis is constructed and how it supports germ cells all the way to functional sperm.

theme: tRNA charging, modification and translational fidelity
story: The core is tRNA aminoacylation in cytosol and mitochondria, which links each tRNA to its amino acid and maintains translational fidelity. tRNA processing and modification members (intron splicing, wobble guanine modification and uridine thiolation, wybutosine at G37 of tRNA-Phe) and selenocysteine synthesis on its own tRNA tune decoding accuracy and expand the code, with translational readthrough as the related decoding outcome. Diphthamide synthesis on EEF2 and peptidyl-histidine modification fit as modifications of the elongation machinery itself, so the cluster describes how the translation apparatus is prepared to decode mRNA accurately.

theme: SLC anion transporters and their mineralization diseases
story: The centre is solute-carrier transport of inorganic anions: SLC26 exchangers (chloride, bicarbonate, iodide, sulfate, oxalate), SLC4 bicarbonate transporters, and SLC34/SLC20 phosphate carriers. Most other members are the inherited diseases of these carriers, including congenital chloride diarrhea, Pendred syndrome, distal and proximal renal tubular acidosis, pulmonary alveolar microlithiasis, basal ganglia calcification and PXE, many of which are disorders of ectopic or deficient mineralization; enamel mineralization, tooth eruption and SLC24A4 amelogenesis imperfecta belong there. SLC24A5 albinism and SLC2A10 arterial tortuosity are other SLC defects grouped by gene family rather than by anion transport, so the cluster is about epithelial ion and phosphate handling and the pathologies of its failure.

theme: Hepatic xenobiotic and steroid biotransformation
story: The core is xenobiotic metabolism, catabolism and toxin breakdown, mediated by cytochrome P450 reactions (CYP1A2 N-hydroxylation of aromatic amines, oxidative demethylation, cytochrome metabolism) and phase II cytosolic sulfonation. Natural-product substrates (alkaloids, phenylpropanoids, monoterpenoids, polyketides) are what these enzymes clear, and steroid metabolism reflects the same P450 and sulfotransferase families acting on endogenous lipids. Together it describes the liver's two-phase chemical modification system that inactivates and eliminates foreign and endogenous lipophilic compounds.

theme: Thymocyte and bone marrow cell number control
story: The cluster is about keeping haematopoietic and lymphoid cell populations at the right size: thymocyte proliferation (positively and negatively regulated), thymocyte survival and T cell differentiation in the thymus are the centre. Proliferation and apoptosis of bone marrow cells provide the upstream compartment that seeds the thymus, and homeostasis of cell number within a tissue is the overall goal. Together it describes how primary lymphoid organs balance proliferation, death and differentiation to produce T cells.

theme: IL-17 axis driving antimicrobial peptide production
story: The centre is interleukin-17 signalling: IL-17 and IL-17A pathways, Th17 lineage commitment, and positive and negative regulation of IL-17 production. Its main output is barrier defence, captured by antibacterial and antimicrobial peptide biosynthesis and regulation of their production, with negative regulation of antibacterial defence as the brake. IL-36 and its antagonist-like IL-38 are IL-1 family epithelial cytokines that amplify or temper the same Th17 and antimicrobial programme, so the cluster describes how type 17 immunity induces epithelial antimicrobial defence.

theme: RAS-MAPK signalling and its oncogenic dysregulation
story: The core is RAS activation and inactivation: SOS-mediated GTP loading, regulation of RAS by GAPs, and negative regulation of Ras signal transduction. Disease members cover how this switch breaks, with RAS GTPase mutants, RAS GAP mutants, NF1 loss of function and MAP2K mutants that hyperactivate the cascade. Downstream readouts and inputs, namely RSK activation, IGF1R-triggered SHC events and AKT inhibition of the TSC complex, place RAS within growth-factor signalling to MAPK and mTOR, so the cluster describes RAS-driven proliferative signalling and the RASopathy/cancer lesions that deregulate it.

theme: Cadherin-based adherens junctions and cell-cell adhesion
story: The core is calcium-dependent cell-cell adhesion through classical cadherins: adherens junction assembly and protein localization there, CDH11 homotypic and heterotypic interactions, and E-cadherin (CDH1) processing, trafficking and degradation. Apoptotic cleavage of adhesion proteins describes how these junctions are dismantled in dying cells, while the generic cell junction and apical junction sets provide the broader junctional complex the cadherins sit in. Together it describes how cadherin junctions are built, maintained and turned over to hold tissues together.

theme: Craniofacial and limb embryonic morphogenesis
story: The cluster centres on shaping the embryonic head and face: neurocranium and viscerocranium morphogenesis, face, nose and anterior head development, and hard and soft palate formation. Forelimb, hindlimb and digit morphogenesis form the parallel appendage programme, and mesenchymal cell development is the shared cellular basis, since both face and limbs are built from patterned mesenchyme (neural crest and lateral plate). Together it describes mesenchyme-driven morphogenesis of the skull, face and limbs.

theme: Arp2/3-driven actin protrusion and cell migration
story: The centre is branched actin network assembly at the leading edge: Rho GTPase activation of WASP and WAVE, positive and negative regulation of Arp2/3 nucleation, actin polymerization, barbed-end capping, severing and depolymerization. These dynamics build the protrusive structures listed, including lamellipodia, ruffles, pseudopodia and podosomes, and macropinocytosis uses the same ruffling machinery. Protein localization to the leading edge, actomyosin contraction and substrate-dependent extension complete the motility cycle, so the cluster describes how cells push forward their membrane to crawl.

theme: Regulatory T cell suppression of T cell responses
story: The core is restraint of T cell activity: negative regulation of activated T cell, CD4 and CD8 proliferation and activation, T cell cytokine and interferon-gamma production, and T cell migration. The mechanism the cluster points to is regulatory T cells, with promotion of CD4+CD25+ Treg differentiation and suppression of Th17 commitment, plus immunoregulation across monocytes and lymphocytes. Positive regulation of CD4 proliferation is the counterweight, so the cluster as a whole describes the balance that limits effector T cell responses and maintains tolerance.

theme: Netrin-mediated axon guidance in neuron subtypes
story: The centre is netrin signalling, both attractive and repulsive (netrin-mediated repulsion, chemorepulsion), steering axons through regulation of axon extension and anterior/posterior guidance. Specific neuronal populations whose projections depend on these cues are named, namely dopaminergic and serotonergic neurons and dorsal root ganglion sensory neurons. Together the cluster describes how midline and longitudinal guidance cues shape the trajectories of particular neuronal classes during wiring of the nervous system.

theme: Glycerolipid synthesis, remodelling and glycerol transport
story: The core is the glycerolipid backbone pathway: synthesis of phosphatidic acid, diacylglycerol and monoacylglycerol, triglyceride biosynthesis and acyl chain remodelling of DAG and TAG. Glycerophospholipid catabolism (hydrolysis of LPC and LPE) feeds and drains the same intermediates, while aquaporin-mediated glycerol transport from adipocytes to liver, glycerol and urea transmembrane transport describe how the glycerol released by lipolysis is moved between tissues (aquaglyceroporins also carry urea). Together the cluster describes how fats are assembled, remodelled and broken down, and how their glycerol backbone circulates.

theme: Neurotrophin Trk receptor signalling
story: The centre is neurotrophin signalling through Trk receptors: NGF/TRKA and NTF3/NTRK3 activation and the adaptor routes downstream of them (FRS2, ARMS, RAS, PI3K, PLCG1). These feed the kinase cascades listed, namely RAS signalling, PI3K/AKT, p38 MAPK and ERK5, which converge on CREB phosphorylation and NGF-stimulated transcription. Together the cluster describes how neurotrophins activate survival, differentiation and gene-expression programmes in neurons.

theme: Heme biosynthesis and iron homeostasis
story: The core is heme synthesis (heme A and B, protoporphyrinogen IX, tetrapyrrole regulation) and its use in hemoglobin production and the heme metabolism programme of erythroid cells. Iron supply sits alongside it, with iron import, response to iron, systemic iron homeostasis, heme scavenging from plasma, heme transport and assimilation, while mitochondrial ABC transporters and cytosolic iron-sulfur cluster assembly reflect the mitochondrial export of iron-containing intermediates. Oxygen detection, superoxide removal and selenium response add the redox context, so the cluster describes how cells acquire iron and build heme, mainly for erythropoiesis.

theme: B cell activation, germinal centre and plasma cell differentiation
story: The core is B cell identity and maturation: naive and memory B cell signatures, B cell surface markers, B cell development and activation, and the descriptive module on lymphocyte activation in lymphoid tissue. The trajectory continues through germinal centre B cell differentiation and plasma cell differentiation to immunoglobulin-secreting plasma cell signatures, with T follicular helper differentiation as the T cell help that drives this. Together the cluster describes the humoral immune response from naive B cell to antibody-producing plasma cell.

theme: Circadian clock transcriptional feedback loop
story: The centre is the core molecular clock: BMAL1 (ARNTL), CLOCK and NPAS2 activating clock-controlled genes, the CRY:PER:kinase complex repressing them, phosphorylation and nuclear translocation of both arms, CRY/PER degradation, and the ROR/REV-ERB loop controlling BMAL1 expression. Entrainment by photoperiod and locomotor rhythm are the input and behavioural output, and negative regulation of circadian rhythm adds its brakes. Clock-controlled physiology (glucocorticoid signalling, cold-induced thermogenesis, pancreatic beta cell proliferation and development) and NPAS4, a paralogous bHLH-PAS activity-dependent factor, show how the clock gates metabolism, so the cluster describes timekeeping and its physiological outputs.

theme: APC/C-mediated mitotic exit
story: The core is the anaphase-promoting complex/cyclosome: APC/C:Cdc20 targeting cyclin A, cyclin B, securin and Nek2A for degradation, APC/C phosphorylation and direct inhibition, the late-anaphase switch to APC/C:Cdh1 and Cdh1 autodegradation. Regulation of exit from mitosis is the outcome these degradation events produce, and aberrant mitotic exit due to RB1 defects is the cancer-related failure mode. Together the cluster describes how ordered ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis drives chromosome separation and return to interphase.

theme: Heart ventricular and septal morphogenesis
story: The centre is building the cardiac ventricles: ventricle formation, right and left ventricular morphogenesis, trabecula formation and compact myocardium maturation, and growth, proliferation and apoptosis that shape the heart. Cell-type members describe its components, namely endocardium differentiation and morphogenesis, ventricular and atrial cardiomyocyte development, sarcomere organization, septum cells and cardiac vascular smooth muscle with coronary vasculogenesis. Mesoderm development and adult heart development bracket the timeline, so the cluster describes how the heart's chambers, walls and septa are formed.

theme: Lymphocyte-regulating cytokines: IL-10, IL-12 family, interferons
story: The core is cytokine signalling that steers lymphocytes, especially NK and NKT cells: IL-12, IL-23, IL-27 and IL-35 (the IL-12 family), IL-15 and IL-21, and regulation of NK and NKT cell activation, proliferation and differentiation. Type I and type III interferon response and production add antiviral signalling sharing JAK-STAT machinery. IL-10 and the IL-20 family (IL-22 and relatives) supply the anti-inflammatory and epithelial-repair arm, linked to negative regulation of inflammation at wounds and epithelial proliferation in healing, so the cluster describes JAK-STAT cytokines that both drive and resolve lymphocyte-mediated inflammation.

theme: Lysosome fusion and endolysosomal size control
story: The centre is delivery of material to lysosomes by membrane fusion: late endosome to lysosome transport, multivesicular body-lysosome fusion, autophagosome-lysosome fusion and vacuole fusion. Regulation of endosome and lysosome size describes the balance of fusion and fission that sets organelle size, and SARS-CoV-2 modulation of autophagy shows a virus blocking this fusion step. Regulation of synaptic vesicle transport is a peripheral neuronal trafficking member, so the cluster is mainly about the terminal fusion steps of the endolysosomal and autophagic routes.

theme: Adipogenesis and transcriptional control of lipid and glucose metabolism
story: The core is adipose tissue development: white fat cell differentiation and proliferation, fat pad development, PPARG-driven adipogenesis with MLL3/MLL4 coactivators, and positive and negative regulation of adipose growth and PPAR signalling. The transcriptional regulators of lipid metabolism, namely LXR (NR1H2/NR1H3) control of lipogenesis, lipolysis and gluconeogenesis, and SREBP activation, govern triglyceride, phospholipid and fatty acid homeostasis. Gluconeogenesis control, caloric restriction, beta cell proliferation, thermogenesis and VLDL remodelling connect this to whole-body energy balance, so the cluster describes nuclear-receptor control of fat storage and systemic metabolism.

theme: RAS-RAF-ERK signalling and its negative feedback
story: The centre is the RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK cascade: SOS activation of RAS, RAF activation (including SHOC2-MRAS complexes), MAP2K and MAPK mutants, and RSK as an ERK target. A large share of members are about turning the pathway off, namely negative feedback regulation of MAPK, ERK inactivation by dual-specificity phosphatase dephosphorylation of threonine and tyrosine, and negative regulation of Ras and ERK signalling. RIT/RIN signalling to p38 adds a parallel small-GTPase route, so the cluster describes MAPK pathway activation, its oncogenic and RASopathy variants, and its feedback termination.

theme: Nucleic acid editing, demethylation and alkylation repair
story: The cluster centres on enzymatic chemical modification of bases in DNA and RNA: ADAR adenosine-to-inosine and APOBEC cytidine-to-uridine editing, oxidative demethylation by ALKBH2/3 reversing alkylation damage, MGMT direct damage reversal, and TET/TDG-mediated 5-methylcytosine demethylation that reactivates CpG islands. An antiviral arm uses the same deaminases, with APOBEC3G restricting retroviral replication (countered by HIV Vif), clearance of foreign nucleic acids and host suppression of viral genomes. Together it describes how cells rewrite base chemistry for repair, epigenetic reprogramming, RNA recoding and viral defence.

theme: Glutamate-centred amino acid and nitrogen metabolism
story: The core is the glutamate/glutamine node: glutamate and glutamine metabolism, 2-oxoglutarate as their carbon skeleton, and conversions to proline, ornithine, arginine and citrulline. Ammonia handling links these, with nitrogen utilization, ammonium homeostasis and response, urea cycle regulation and the SLC25A15 ornithine carrier defect causing HHH syndrome. Aspartate/asparagine metabolism, proline catabolism and GABA degradation connect via transamination, so the cluster describes how amino acid nitrogen is shuttled through glutamate and disposed of via the urea cycle.

theme: Amino acid catabolism: aromatic, threonine and proline
story: The centre is amino acid breakdown, especially phenylalanine and tyrosine catabolism (with phenylketonuria and the tetrahydrobiopterin cofactor needed for phenylalanine hydroxylation), threonine catabolism to glycine and proline catabolism. Glyoxylate, aldehyde and non-proteinogenic amino acid catabolism and mitochondrial/peroxisomal metabolism describe where the resulting intermediates go. Many members are broad, now-obsolete parent terms for organic acid, amide and alpha-amino acid metabolism, which here simply frame the cluster as general amino acid catabolism with its inherited metabolic disorders.

theme: Incretin and nutrient GPCR control of insulin secretion
story: The core is regulation of insulin secretion by G protein-coupled receptors on islet beta cells: GLP-1 and GIP synthesis, secretion and signalling, glucagon-type ligand receptors, fatty acid receptor FFAR1/GPR40, and acetylcholine. Free fatty acid and hydroxycarboxylic acid receptors are nutrient-sensing GPCRs, adenylate cyclase activation is the shared cAMP route, and somatostatin receptor signalling is the inhibitory counterpart. Glucagon response and growth hormone secretion extend this to other endocrine hormones, so the cluster describes how gut and nutrient signals tune hormone secretion through GPCRs.

theme: Lipoprotein remodelling and cholesterol efflux in macrophages
story: The centre is reverse cholesterol transport: HDL assembly and remodelling, ABC transporter-mediated cholesterol and phospholipid efflux, LXR (NR1H3/NR1H2) induction of efflux genes, and regulation of HDL clearance. The macrophage side covers LDL remodelling, oxidised LDL responses, cholesterol import and storage, pinocytosis and foam cell differentiation, which is what happens when uptake outpaces efflux. Together the cluster describes how lipoproteins move cholesterol into and out of cells, with the balance determining foam cell formation in atherosclerosis.

theme: Islet hormone secretion by incretins and nutrients
story: The core is pancreatic islet hormone release: glucose-stimulated insulin secretion and its positive and negative regulation, glucagon secretion and response, and the beta cell programme. Incretins (GLP-1, GIP), acetylcholine, fatty acid receptors (FFAR1/GPR40, free fatty acid and hydroxycarboxylic acid receptors) and glucagon-type receptors act through adenylate cyclase to amplify secretion, while somatostatin signalling inhibits it. Growth hormone secretion shows the same GPCR logic in another endocrine cell, so the cluster describes how islets integrate nutrient, gut and neural signals to set insulin and glucagon output.

theme: Actin cytoskeleton remodelling for protrusions and motility
story: The centre is actin filament dynamics: polymerization and depolymerization, Arp2/3 nucleation, barbed-end capping, severing, crosslinking and parallel bundle assembly. These build the protrusions listed, namely lamellipodia, filopodia (positively and negatively regulated), ruffles and pseudopodia, with leading-edge localization, cell polarity and actin-based motility as outcomes. RHOF GTPase cycle and EPHB forward signalling are upstream regulators, postsynaptic actin organization applies this to dendritic spines, and caspase cleavage of cytoskeletal proteins is its dismantling in apoptosis.

theme: Inflammasomes and pyroptotic host defence
story: The core is inflammasome-triggered pyroptosis: AIM2 and IPAF (NLRC4) inflammasomes, non-canonical CASP4/CASP5 inflammasomes sensing intracellular LPS and their substrate cleavage (gasdermin D), and pyroptotic cell death and inflammation. Detection of bacteria and GBP-mediated host defence are upstream steps that expose bacterial ligands to these sensors. Enterobacterial factors antagonizing host defence and defective pyroptosis describe how pathogens or mutations disable the pathway, so the cluster as a whole is the cytosolic sensing-and-killing response to intracellular bacteria.

theme: Chondrocyte differentiation and endochondral ossification
story: The centre is the cartilage lineage: cartilage condensation, chondroblast differentiation, chondrocyte proliferation and differentiation (positive and negative regulation), growth plate development and hypertrophy, with RUNX2 driving maturation. Replacement (endochondral) ossification is where this cartilage template ends up, while direct (intramembranous) ossification, mesenchymal stem cell differentiation and tendon development are sibling fates from the same skeletal mesenchyme. Together it describes how mesenchymal progenitors form cartilage and bone during skeletal growth.

theme: Kidney development via ureteric bud and nephric duct
story: The core is early kidney organogenesis: intermediate mesoderm formation, nephric duct formation, ureteric bud induction, outgrowth, elongation and branching, and ureter morphogenesis. The metanephric mesenchyme counterpart is covered by mesenchymal stem cell maintenance, protection from apoptosis, mesenchymal-to-epithelial transition and metanephric tubule formation. Organ induction and epithelial tube formation describe the reciprocal signalling between bud and mesenchyme, so the cluster describes how the urinary collecting system and nephrons arise together.

theme: Microtubule-based organelle transport in neurons
story: The centre is long-range intracellular transport along microtubules and actin: plus-end-directed organelle transport, anterograde and retrograde dense core vesicle transport, synaptic vesicle cytoskeletal transport and vesicle transport along actin. In neurons this distributes cargo to distant compartments, with axonal transport of mitochondria, axo-dendritic protein transport, delivery of neurotransmitter receptors to dendrites and protein localization to presynapses. Regulation of endosome and lysosome size and mitochondrial distribution reflect organelle positioning, so the cluster describes how motor-driven transport supplies and maintains synapses.

theme: Endosomal recycling and secretory membrane traffic
story: The core is endosomal trafficking: endosome organization, early to late endosome transport, endocytic and receptor recycling, endosome-to-plasma membrane transport, plasma membrane to endosome transport and endosomal membrane tubulation. The secretory side covers Golgi vesicle budding, constitutive secretion, protein localization to Golgi membrane and membrane docking, and the descriptive module ties these together through COPII export, EEA1-marked endosomes, SNARE/SM fusion, phosphoinositide-dependent uncoating and SPAST-mediated tubule shaping. The cluster describes the general machinery that moves cargo and membrane between the ER, Golgi, endosomes and the cell surface.

theme: Fibroblast and stromal extracellular matrix programmes
story: The centre is the fibroblast/stromal compartment: resident perivascular fibroblasts producing matrix (tenascin C, collagens, TGF-beta family members), and the mechanoresponsive YAP/TAZ programme whose outputs CCN1/CCN2 and caveolin-1 mark activated stroma. Fibroblast proliferation and focal adhesion assembly describe the cell behaviours behind matrix remodelling, and plasma membrane signal transduction supplies the growth-factor and mechanical inputs. Together the cluster describes how connective tissue cells sense tension and growth signals to build and remodel extracellular matrix.

theme: COPII and COPI ER-Golgi vesicle traffic
story: The core is the early secretory pathway: COPII coat assembly, cargo loading and concentration at ER exit sites and ER-to-Golgi vesicle transport. COPI vesicle budding and Golgi-to-ER retrograde traffic are the return route that recycles escaped ER proteins and transport machinery, and the ER membrane protein set captures the cargo and residents involved. Together the cluster describes the bidirectional vesicle shuttle that moves newly made proteins out of the ER while retrieving ER components.

theme: Collagen and elastic fibre extracellular matrix assembly
story: The centre is fibrillar extracellular matrix: collagen biosynthesis and its positive regulation, collagen fibril organization and crosslinking (by lysyl oxidases). Elastic fibre assembly and elastic fibre-associated molecules add the elastic component of connective tissue, and the several extracellular matrix gene sets summarize the coexpressed matrix programme. Together the cluster describes how connective tissue builds its load-bearing collagen and elastic fibres.

theme: DNA replication initiation and S-phase checkpoint control
story: The core is DNA replication during the cell cycle: initiation of DNA-templated replication, positive and negative regulation of nuclear replication, and mitotic DNA replication, with E2F1 targets supplying the G1/S transcriptional programme for the replication machinery. Checkpoint members (ATR activation under replication stress, the intra-S DNA damage and DNA replication checkpoints) monitor this process and halt it when forks stall. Resolution of recombination intermediates describes the clean-up needed after fork repair, so the cluster as a whole describes licensing, firing and surveillance of genome duplication.
